div.l: That is to seye / that telleth in this caas
Talis of sentence / and most solas
Shalhaue a souper at our althir cost
Here in this place / syttyng bi this post
Whanne that ye comyn / ageyn fro Cantirbury
And for to make you / the more mery
I wol my selve goodly / wᵗith. you ryde
Vpon my own cost and be your guyde
And who so wol my /Iugement wᵗith seye
Shal pay al that ye spendyn by the wey
And if that ye vooche saaf / that it be so
Telle me a noon / wythouten wordys moo
And y wol yerly / shape me therfore
This thyng was graunted / and our wothis swore
Wyth wel glad hert / and preyden him also
That he wolde wuche saaf / it for to doo
And that he wolde be / our gouernour
And of our talys / Iuge and reportour
And set a souper / at a certeyn prys
And we wol rewled be / at his devys
In hye and lowe / and thus bi oon assent
We beth accorded / to the Iugement
And thervpon / the wyn was fet a noon
We dronkyn / and to reste wentyn eủerychon
Wythoute any lenger taryynge
A morowe whan the day gan to sprynge
Vp roos our host / and was on alderis cok
And gadered vs to gedir / in a flok
And forth. we redyn / lytyl more than a paas
Vnto the watteryng / of seynt Thomas
And ther our host / bi gan his arreste
And seid lordes / herkenyth yf ye leste
Ye wetyn your forward / and your record
Yif evesong / and morowe song a cord
Lat se who shall telle / the first tale
As ever mot I drynke wyn or ale
